description:
`sh -c` and `bash -c`, which run a script string through this same shell as a child.

In the oracle image `sh` is BusyBox ash, not bash; these cases use only behaviour the two agree
on. Usage errors, which each shell words differently, are covered by the unit tests.

cases.name: sh: child exit status, cwd and variables stay inside
cases.script: cd /tmp; sh -c 'cd /; x=1; exit 3'; echo status=$? pwd=$PWD x=${x-unset}

cases.name: bash: -e stops at the first failure
bash: -u sets the nounset option
cases.script: bash -uc 'case $- in *u*) echo nounset;; esac; echo "${nope-default}"'

cases.name: sh: script read from stdin with -s
find: exec sh -c per file
cases.script: mkdir -p /tmp/shx && cd /tmp/shx && touch 'a b' c && find . -type f -exec sh -c 'echo "<$1>"' _ {} \; | sort

cases.name: find: exec bash -c batch
cases.script: mkdir -p /tmp/shy && cd /tmp/shy && touch x y z && find . -type f -exec bash -c 'echo $#' _ {} +
